summary: Iteration 5 — Nexus AI v4 autonomous reply loop (Claude Sonnet 4.5 buyer-reply simulation + AI-drafted contextual follow-up + human-in-the-loop review queue). Wrote test_nexus_v4.py with 10 tests covering simulate-reply happy path, 404 cases, user scoping, queue enrichment, stats shape, send as-is, send with overrides, 409 on already-sent, dismiss + 404 on re-dismiss. ALL 10 v4 tests PASS. Frontend Playwright verified: /app/replies loads with stats + draft cards, sidebar nav-replies sits between nav-onboarding and nav-outbox, Outbox shows simulate-reply buttons on BOTH promote.intro AND reply.followup emails, button cycles 'Simulate buyer reply' → 'Claude thinking…' → auto-nav to /app/replies, Edit swaps to textareas, Dismiss removes card + decrements pending. Regression: dashboard, pipeline, subscribe, outbox, onboarding all load clean (no DOM errors). v3 regression suite 14/14 still pass.

minor.issue: Default limit=25 caps the activity feed. test_nexus_v2.py::test_promote_creates_deal_and_logs_activity asserts len_after >= len_before+1 without raising the limit, so after the v4 tests added activities the demo user's feed sits at the 25-row cap and the assertion fails (FALSE-POSITIVE regression). The promote endpoint itself still writes the activity correctly — verified via test_promote_twice_idempotent which passes. Suggest either raising default limit or fixing the v2 test to query ?limit=200.

action_items: OPTIONAL: bump default limit on /api/dashboard/activity from 25 → e.g. 100, OR update test_nexus_v2.py::test_promote_creates_deal_and_logs_activity to call /dashboard/activity?limit=200 so it remains stable as activity volume grows. Not blocking — the underlying feature is correct.
critical_code_review_comments: GOOD: simulate_reply (server.py L916-1014) correctly resolves company/contact from deal_doc OR target_doc fallback; persists EmailReply + ReplyDraft with matching reply_id; fires Activity + Slack 'reply.received'; strips ```json``` code fences before JSON parsing — robust.

GOOD: send_draft (L1037-1089) clamps probability with max(0, min(100, ...)); sets agent_status='closing' only when sentiment=='positive'; persists overridden subject/body into the draft doc so subsequent reads reflect what was actually sent; uses send_email() helper which writes kind='reply.followup' to email_outbox with mocked=true. Idempotency guard returns 409 on non-pending status — verified.

GOOD: list_drafts (L1017-1029) and dismiss_draft (L1092-1100) both scoped by user_id; dismiss uses update_one with status='pending' filter so re-dismissing a sent/dismissed draft returns 404 cleanly (atomic check-and-set).

GOOD: Replies.jsx uses Promise.all for /queue + /stats parallel fetch; DraftCard re-fetches list after send/dismiss for fresh state; sentiment-colored borders and intent labels are consistent with backend enum values.

GOOD: Outbox.jsx simulate button is correctly gated on (kind==='promote.intro' || kind==='reply.followup'), shows 'Claude thinking…' during await, then 700ms grace navigate to /app/replies — UX smooth.

MINOR: server.py is now 1168 lines (was 908 in iter_4 + ~260 lines of v4 code). Still no router split. Recommend extracting /api/replies/* and /api/notifications/email/{id}/simulate-reply into a dedicated replies_router.py module.

MINOR: simulate_reply uses session_id=f'reply-{email_id}-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}' — guarantees uniqueness but ALSO means LLM conversation history is never reused across retries. Fine for current spec (one-shot generation), but if retry-with-context is ever needed this would need rework.

MINOR: send_draft does NOT validate that payload.subject/body are non-empty when provided. If a user POSTs {subject: '', body: ''} the empty strings will be sent. Consider treating empty string the same as None (i.e. fall back to draft default).

MINOR: dismiss_draft only matches status='pending'; a draft that was sent then dismissed never hits — that's correct, but the 404 message 'Draft not found or already actioned' could be more specific. Non-blocking.

success_rate.backend: 100% v4 (10/10) — v2 regression 13/14 (1 pre-existing test fragility on /dashboard/activity limit, not a v4 bug) — v3 regression 15/15
success_rate.frontend: 100% — /app/replies + /app/outbox + nav order + simulate-reply→nav + Edit toggle + Dismiss action all verified; dashboard/pipeline/subscribe/onboarding all load clean

test_credentials: Demo session token: demo_session_token_persistent (Bearer header or cookie). See /app/memory/test_credentials.md. Second user (for scoping tests) seeded inline in test_nexus_v4.py via direct Mongo insert and cleaned up via module teardown.
seed_data_creation: Demo user now has 2 pending drafts in /app/replies (one pre-existing Velocity Revenue Partners + one from simulate test), 8 buyer replies received total, 4 follow-ups sent. Outbox has 9 simulate-reply buttons visible (3 promote.intro + 6 reply.followup). Second user (TEST_V4_user_*) was cleaned up after tests.
context_for_next_testing_agent: test_nexus_v4.py is idempotent — each non-readonly test creates a fresh draft by simulating reply on an as-yet-unsimulated promote.intro email. simulate-reply hits real Claude Sonnet 4.5 (~10-25s per call) so tests take ~30-90s; 3 of 10 tests call the LLM. If demo user runs out of fresh promote.intro emails, test_send_with_overrides + test_dismiss_pending_draft will pytest.skip cleanly. Replies UI dismiss action verified working: cards 2→1, pending 2→1. The /dashboard/activity?limit=25 default is the root cause of the only v2 regression failure — main agent's call whether to bump default or update the test query string.
rca of the issue: No real bugs in v4. The single test failure in test_nexus_v2.py::test_promote_creates_deal_and_logs_activity is a pre-existing test fragility, not a v4 regression: that test asserts the activity feed grew by ≥1 after a new promote, but /api/dashboard/activity defaults limit=25 (server.py L535). After v4 tests added ~10 new 'Buyer replied' + 'Reply sent' activities for the demo user, the feed is now permanently at the 25-row cap, so len_after == len_before == 25, breaking the assertion. The promote endpoint itself still inserts the activity correctly — verified by checking /api/dashboard/metrics activities_24h counter increments, and by test_promote_twice_idempotent passing. Fix is one of: (a) raise the activity endpoint default limit, (b) update the test to use ?limit=200, or (c) delete demo user's older activities before the test.
